subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a six-wheeled heavy military carrier with a turreted railgun and deployable outrigger legs, keeping the low-poly sci-fi design mostly static but possibly adding a couple of joints for the turret and gun articulation.

I'll settle on roughly 9m length, 3m width, and 3.5m height with the gun mounted, keeping both the wheels and lowered stabiliser legs touching the ground for a braced stance. For materials I'm planning an olive drab and dark steel camo paint scheme with cyan glow accents for the rail coils and lights, plus hazard decals for surface detail.

Now I'm working out wheel and leg placement along the hull's length—six wheels across three axles toward the front and rear, with stabiliser legs positioned between them, adjusting the z-coordinates until the spacing matches the overall chassis proportions.

Modeling wheels as rotated cylinders with hubs and bolts, then adding fender boxes over each wheel pair to form the arches.

Now shaping the hull as a main box with a sloped upper deck, extruding a side profile to build the cab's angled front and roofline.

Still defining hull and cab geometry...

I'm positioning side windows on the cab sides with a subtle glow, then adding finishing details like a roof sensor mast, light bar, front bumper wedge, glowing headlight boxes, and a front grille.

Now I'm working out the mirror arms and turret setup: a turntable ring near the deck, a rotating turret base, and the railgun assembly. For the rest pose I'm checking clearance so the gun, elevated and pointing forward over the cab, doesn't collide with the cab roof given its length and mount height.

I settle on a 10° elevation angle for the gun and compute the pivot position and direction vector for the muzzle. Now I'm sketching the gun's twin parallel rail boxes, spaced apart and oriented along that direction, using the rod/frustum box helper to build the geometry...

Still building geometry helpers...

Working out the turret body dimensions and placement, then setting the pivot point for the gun cradle at the top of the turret, with side arm plates extending out from it.

Running the gun rail geometry forward to check overall barrel length and elevation height — ends up around 12m long and 5.2m tall at max elevation, which seems reasonable for a heavy carrier. Now I'm adding turret details: ammo box, hatch ring, antenna, sensor dome, smoke launchers, vent grills, and emblem decals.

I'm laying out the rear deck equipment behind the turret — glowing power cells in a cage, cable sweeps, and a reactor housing with vented glow — plus hazard stripe decals, then positioning the four stabilizer legs with bracket, diagonal arm, hydraulic piston, and ground pad geometry.

Still writing leg geometry... now adding foot pad resting positions, wheel placement touching the floor, and fender boxes over each axle.

I'm adding an axle beam spanning the hull width, then considering whether to place side tool lockers between the front and rear wheels, checking clearances so they don't collide with the wheels or mounting legs.

I'll extend the hull to -5.4 and push rear legs to -5.1, keeping pistons at x=2.9, then update the axle positions to 3.4, -2.2, and -3.8. Now I'm working on the cab front details — adding a bumper box with tow hooks, shaping the hull's front slope toward the headlight area, and placing glowing headlight boxes near the front face.

I'm planning seven texture assets: an emblem, hazard stripes, a visor glass gradient with HUD lines, a grille pattern, a serial plate reading "RG-06," a vent design, and a high-voltage warning label, then figuring out how to attach these as decals onto the model's parts.

Now I'm working out the orientation math for side-face decals -- determining which way "up" and "right" point on the left side panel so the text reads correctly when viewed from that angle.

For the paint job, I'm setting up a camo pattern using olive, dark olive, and tan patches with tight gaps so they blend into solid mottled regions, then layering a panelled hull texture with subtle rivets on top for the metal surface detail.

I'll use an iron metal shader for the gun, importing it from the clockwork kit. For the wheels, I'm planning tire tread by painting stripes along the cylinder's circumference using the UV coordinates, then distinguishing the cap faces from the sidewall by checking the normal's axis alignment so the tread pattern only appears on the rolling surface.

For the hub, I'm layering a steel cylinder base with a smaller center cap and adding six bolt cylinders arranged in a ring around the outer face, positioning each by angle offsets in the plane perpendicular to the axle.

Tallying up total part counts across wheels, fenders, legs, hull, cab, turret, gun, rear equipment, and decals to stay comfortably under the 1000-part budget — landing around 250 estimated parts. Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders to streamline part creation with consistent color and placement options.

Setting up the gun's pivot geometry — defining the elevation angle, direction vector, and up vector so parts along the barrel can be positioned using a local coordinate system based on slide distance, lateral offset, and vertical offset from the pivot. Still writing helper functions...

Now I'm laying out the rail pairs symmetrically on either side, then adding thin glowing cyan strips inset along their inner faces to suggest energy conduits, before moving on to the breech block.

Writing coil assembly geometry...

Still placing details...

Checking the gun pivot placement relative to the breech and turret top, the breech center ends up embedded slightly into the turret roof, which reads as properly mounted rather than floating. I'm now placing the turret ring cylinder near the turret's center point.

Working out the turret ring's exact position relative to the hull deck top so it sits flush, then moving on to surface details — emblem decals on the turret sides and angled smoke launcher cylinders positioned near the turret's forward face.

Now I'm placing the smoke launcher clusters along the turret shoulders, plus a hatch with a ring lid, a commander's cupola topped by a sensor dome, and starting a lathe-based rear radar dish profile.

I'm adding thin rear antenna masts with glowing red tips, then roughing out a rear reactor housing box with glowing vent plates and three vertical cyan-glowing cell tubes on top.

Now I'm placing hazard decals and taillight glow boxes on the rear hull face, plus a tow hitch, and sketching side details like vent decals and a serial plate on the cab doors.

I'm adding emblems to the turret sides and reactor rear, hazard stripe textures around the pistons, and side window visor planes on the cab, along with a slanted windscreen texture and roof features like a light bar, sensor ball, and mirror rods.

Now I'm working on the under-armor and front details: a bumper box, tow hooks, a winch roller cylinder, and headlight placements positioned on the bumper front face.

Settling grille plane position, then thinking about the cab front glow slit placement relative to the sloped hull top, adjusting the cab's bottom edge to overlap properly. Now moving on to defining the leg bracket geometry with its mounting box dimensions.

Still writing leg geometry...

Still placing struts and checking clearances...I'm verifying the sleeve overlaps the arm correctly and considering adding side locker boxes near the wheels for visual detail.

For the fenders, I realize the front and rear wheel coverage areas overlap enough to merge into one long tandem fender spanning roughly -4.75 to -1.25, so I'll build that as a single piece rather than two separate ones, plus the standalone front fender from 2.45 to 4.35. I'm now positioning a second locker box near the leg arm area around z=-0.2.

I'm checking clearances for the second locker, the mud flaps behind the rear wheels, and the leg bracket positions to make sure none of these pieces intersect the wheels or sleeve geometry.

For the axle beams, I'm sizing a box per axle positioned so it sits above the hull bottom and clears the wheels, and deciding to skip the differential housing sphere and underside skirt panels for simplicity, while noting the camo texture adds some paint overhead but should still be fine.

Then I need the glow import for flat-colored or textured parts since paint itself can't glow. I'm defining the palette—olive, dark, steel, cyan, yellow, red, rubber—and starting to lay out texture SVGs for the emblem (circle with star and chevron) and the visor (teal gradient rect with diagonal reflection highlights).

Writing hazard, grille, serial textures...

Now sketching the vent with glowing cyan slats, a warning sign with a lightning bolt, then setting up the final import structure for the build script.

I'm defining camo patches for panels and a tarnished steel material, trimming unused imports down to just what I need, and planning mud wear details next.

Writing weather blend function...

Now I'm starting the railgun carrier build, setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and decals to construct the model piece by piece.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Rear axles go at z -2.2 and -3.8. I'm placing antennas as thin rods near the cab with glowing red tips, sizing a cab roof sensor sphere plus an amber light bar with several glow cells across the roof, and considering whether to add handrails or a cable sweep before deciding to skip the ladder detail.

I'm adding two sagging power cables with a dark matte finish running from the reactor to the turret using catmull curve sweeps, plus glowing cylinder cells on the reactor top and a four-post cage frame around it. I'm also placing emblem decals on both sides of the turret, sized to fit the turret's thickness, and weighing whether to add a hazard or warning label near the gun breech or reactor.

Placing a warning decal on each reactor side, a vent on the reactor's rear face with a glow, and a hazard stripe along the lower rear of the hull, then checking that each decal's facing direction matches its surface so the texture reads correctly from the viewer's side. Now defining a helper function for computing ground positions with latitude and elevation offsets.
